solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Deluded father jogged round with one athletic club (9)

blocks.note: AC = athletic club, as in club names

annotation.surface: A father with delusions of fitness goes for a jog round the track with his athletic club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deluded' sits at the front looking like a description of the jogging father; it is the definition, and the rest is five small pieces laid end to end.
annotation.definitionFit: Here the noun for a sufferer serves as an adjective: paranoia is a mental disorder marked by fixed false beliefs of persecution.

entries.clue: Headgear chap praying could perhaps provide (8,3)

indicatorNotes.could perhaps provide: the letters of 'chap praying', if rearranged, could provide the answer: a hedged offer of new letters

annotation.surface: A man at prayer might be wearing some particular hat.
annotation.walkthrough: A PHRYGIAN CAP is the soft conical cap with the tip bent forward, worn as a symbol of liberty in revolutionary France.
annotation.definitionFit: Specific example of a general class: the soft red conical bonnet of French revolutionaries, named after ancient Phrygia in Anatolia.

entries.clue: Fiddle lazily and with a stiff style (7)

blocks.note: to rig = to fiddle, as with results

annotation.surface: A violinist plays lazily and yet stiffly, which is an odd combination.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' reads as a violin to be played; here it is the verb meaning to cheat or rig.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain paraphrase of the adverb: acting inflexibly, without bending, is doing things in an unyielding manner.

entries.clue: Drug smuggler’s refusal to carry Arabian cocaine at first (5)

indicatorNotes.to carry: NO carries the other letters inside it, as a bag carries its load
indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of cocaine is wanted

annotation.surface: A drug smuggler refuses to carry an Arab's cocaine.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal, chiefly American slang, shortened from narcotics, for a trafficker in cartels such as those of Mexico and Colombia.

entries.clue: Hesitating? Sure loiter about (10)

indicatorNotes.about: letters knocked about, scattered around, end up rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone hanging about undecided is asked if they are hesitating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sure' looks like confident reassurance, the opposite of hesitating, and is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone unable to make up their mind wavers, and wavering is what hesitating means.

entries.clue: What’s pulled wife out of bad car wreck? (7)

indicatorNotes.out of: W, the wife, is taken out of the fodder before it is jumbled
indicatorNotes.bad: letters in a bad way are in poor order, so rearrange them

blocks.note: CAR WRECK less W; anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A question about who got a wife out of a car crash, and what pulled her clear.
annotation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart by two people so it bangs, a British festive tradition. 'Pulled' looks like a rescue from the wreck.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by custom: at British Christmas dinners two people tug the ends of this paper tube until it snaps with a bang.

entries.clue: Bad quality insulin sent as ordered (13)

indicatorNotes.as ordered: the letters are put in order, arranged afresh as if on instruction

annotation.surface: A complaint that the insulin delivered as ordered was of poor quality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad quality' reads as a verdict on the insulin; it is a moral quality, the opposite of saintliness.
annotation.definitionFit: A moral trait rather than poor workmanship: failing to be holy or virtuous is a character flaw.

entries.clue: Bad timing relating to a point in harmony (13)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one word inside another: PUNCTUAL sits in UNITY

blocks.note: punctual in its old geometric sense, relating to a point

annotation.surface: A musician's bad timing concerns one point in the harmony.
annotation.walkthrough: PUNCTUAL comes from Latin punctum, a point, and still means 'relating to a point' in geometry; the musical surface hides that sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: arriving late, failing to keep appointments on schedule, is a habit of poor timekeeping.

entries.clue: Cards cheat takes in two bridge players — it gives an edge (9)

indicatorNotes.takes in: to take in is to admit inside, so SHARPER holds EN

blocks.note: a card sharper cheats at cards
East and North, two of the four bridge seats

annotation.surface: A card cheat recruits two bridge players to give himself an advantage at the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gives an edge' reads as giving the cheat an advantage; the definition means literally putting an edge on a blade.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal description: a whetstone or pencil tool hones blades and points so they cut keenly.

entries.clue: Instant everything is set in position (7)

blocks.note: inst. = instant, meaning of this month, in old business letters

annotation.surface: In an instant everything is in place.
annotation.walkthrough: INST is the abbreviation for 'instant' in the old letter-writing sense, 'your letter of the 5th inst.', meaning this month.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: fitting equipment or placing someone formally in office both mean putting them where they belong.

entries.clue: Confused about European banker’s small car (5-7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so THREW goes around E

blocks.note: threw = confused, as in 'the question threw me'
something that banks, or leans over, heels; so a heeler

annotation.surface: A confused story about a European banker who drives a small car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banker' wants to be someone in finance; here it is anything that banks, tilting like a ship that heels. The 's is 'is', the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Example of the class: vehicles like the Reliant Robin, a British economy runabout with a single front wheel.

entries.clue: Execute one parliamentarian — permit having fellows enter (9)

indicatorNotes.having: LET is having, holding, the fellows inside it
indicatorNotes.enter: the fellows enter, go into, the word for permit

annotation.surface: A grim scene: an MP to be executed, with men let in to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Execute' sounds like a death sentence for the parliamentarian; it means to carry out a plan.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of carrying out a plan or policy, not killing anyone.

entries.clue: Entertainer’s beginning with joke outfit (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here the E

annotation.surface: An entertainer starts out with a comic outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' reads as a costume noun; it is the verb, to kit out.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to supply someone with the gear or clothing they need.

entries.clue: Excess cool — illness unknown after it? (11)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' fixes the order: the unknown comes after IT

annotation.surface: Someone who overdid staying cool asks whether an unknown illness followed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like temperature beside an illness; it is the slang word for great, SUPER.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an amount beyond what is needed, a surplus or overabundance.

entries.clue: Received a name (5)

blocks.note: a common English man's first name

annotation.surface: Someone was given a name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Received a name' reads as one event, being named; it splits into two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Radio operators confirm a message this way, the letter R once being spoken so in phonetic alphabets; it is also a man's forename.

entries.clue: One making review cut pay increase in public relations (11)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one word inside another: RAISE sits in PR

blocks.note: to reap is to cut a crop
a raise is a pay increase

annotation.surface: Someone reviewing a PR department cuts its pay rise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut pay increase' reads as a single idea, cutting a raise; 'cut' is its own piece, REAP.
annotation.definitionFit: Agent noun: a person who assesses something again, weighing its value afresh, is carrying out a review.

entries.clue: Full fruit pie that is consumed (5)

indicatorNotes.consumed: what is consumed is eaten up and gone, so IE vanishes from PIE

blocks.note: PIE with IE (that is) consumed leaves P

annotation.surface: Eating a fruit pie leaves you full.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That is' is IE, the Latin id est; take it away from PIE.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym for rounded and well filled out, as in cheeks, cushions or figures.

entries.clue: Neglected Saturn, say, because of interest by Newton (11)

indicatorNotes.by: 'by' means next to, so the N is set beside the rest

blocks.note: for the sake of, in the interest of: FOR SAKE
N = newton, the unit of force

annotation.surface: Saturn is neglected because Newton's interest lay elsewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saturn' and 'Newton' pull toward astronomy and physics; Saturn is the god, and Newton gives only the unit symbol N.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes a dismal, remote place that seems abandoned even by heaven, so uncared for.

entries.clue: Very good quick look round protected by fellow UN soldier (11)

indicatorNotes.round: turned round, the quick look faces the other way
indicatorNotes.protected by: the pieces are protected by being wrapped inside the fellow

blocks.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal
PEEK, a quick look, turned round

annotation.surface: A fellow UN soldier sneaks a good look round while under protection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fellow UN soldier' reads as one phrase; 'fellow' belongs to the wordplay and only 'UN soldier' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: The blue-helmeted troops sent by the United Nations to monitor ceasefires carry this job title.

entries.clue: Hideous newborn’s masculine when undressed (7)

indicatorNotes.when undressed: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so the end letters go

blocks.note: BABY'S, a newborn's, with its first letter stripped off
MALE, with its last letter stripped off

annotation.surface: An unkind remark that a baby boy looks hideous without his clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words are joined first, BABYSMALE, and only the outermost letters of the whole string come off, one at each end.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: dreadful, appallingly bad, originally meaning as deep as an abyss.

entries.clue: Gathering rising support within imperial dynasty (7)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so TEE flips
indicatorNotes.within: 'within' puts the reversed support inside MING

blocks.note: the Ming dynasty of imperial China
a TEE supports a golf ball; rising, it reads EET

annotation.surface: Support for an imperial dynasty is growing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising support' reads as growing popularity; it is a tee turned upward in a down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an assembly of people come together for a purpose.

entries.clue: Genuine about element of part of the eye (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so REAL wraps round TIN

annotation.surface: A real question about some component of the eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like part of the eye's makeup; it is a chemical element, TIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for the retina, the light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eyeball.

entries.clue: Attentive hospital required removing third of fingers (7)

indicatorNotes.removing: removing takes something away, here one letter out of NEEDFUL
indicatorNotes.third of: the third of a word is its third letter, the N of fiNgers

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs
the third letter of fiNgers is N; remove it from NEEDFUL

annotation.surface: A hospital needs an attentive surgeon to remove part of a finger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Removing third of fingers' sounds like amputation; it asks you to drop the N, the third letter of 'fingers'.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: taking heed means paying close notice, being mindful and careful.

entries.clue: Plan beneficial to drug smuggler concealing a ton (9)

indicatorNotes.concealing: to conceal is to hide inside, so MULE hides A T

blocks.note: for = in favour of, beneficial to
a mule carries drugs across borders

annotation.surface: A drug smuggler hides a ton of goods as part of a plan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plan' reads as a noun, the smuggler's scheme; it is the verb, to formulate.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: devising a strategy or working out the details systematically.

entries.clue: Workers in group sadly get meaner pay deal (10,9)

indicatorNotes.sadly: letters treated sadly are in a sorry state, so jumbled up

blocks.note: a collective is a group of workers

annotation.surface: A group of workers grows sadly meaner over a pay deal.
annotation.walkthrough: A collective agreement is a pay deal struck by a union for all its members, which fits the surface's workers and their grievance.
annotation.definitionFit: Industrial-relations term for wages and conditions negotiated by a trade union on behalf of all its members.

entries.clue: Hero trained with Resistance, one presenting with pride (4-5)

blocks.note: a lion is a hero, a brave person

annotation.surface: A trained Resistance hero proudly presents himself.
annotation.walkthrough: A group of lions is a pride, so 'presenting with pride' describes a circus lion-tamer's act, not someone proud of their work.
annotation.definitionFit: Pun on the collective noun: a circus performer stages an act alongside a group of big cats.

entries.clue: Class diversity in music-hall entertainment (7)

blocks.note: a class or kind, as botanists rank a plant below species
the British stage tradition of mixed acts: songs, comics, jugglers

annotation.surface: A range of social classes is found in music-hall entertainment.
annotation.walkthrough: In fact a triple definition: 'diversity' is a third meaning of VARIETY. Music hall was Victorian British popular theatre of songs and comic acts.
annotation.definitionFit: One word covers a subdivision or type, and the mixed bill of singers and comedians on the Victorian popular stage.

entries.clue: Expel former heart-throb? (7)

blocks.note: a pulse is literally a throb of the heart

annotation.surface: Throw out the former heart-throb?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heart-throb' means a pin-up in the surface, and is taken literally in the wordplay: the throb of the heart, a pulse.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic verb from the same Latin root, expulsare, meaning to drive out or eject.

entries.clue: North African pop with a lot of attack (3)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so drop the last letter

blocks.note: a sudden assault on a target (4 letters), losing its final D

annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a dad; it is pop music, and rai is the popular music of Algeria.
annotation.definitionFit: Genre name: an Algerian folk-derived popular music style, made famous internationally by singers like Khaled.

entries.clue: Wordy part for actor lacking English in pictures (6)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Wordy' fits the actor's part so well it seems a description of the script; it is the definition on its own.

entries.clue: Artist dividing using shade (6)

indicatorNotes.dividing: something dividing a word splits it by sitting in the middle

blocks.note: with = using, as in 'cut with a knife'

annotation.walkthrough: 'Shade' sits beside 'artist' as a painting term; it means a ghost.
annotation.definitionFit: Both words name a ghost or spectral apparition, the shade being the classical term for a departed spirit.

entries.clue: Male with natural head for cruelty (13)

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Sheerness

annotation.surface: A man with a natural bent for cruelty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland, a NESS; 'natural head' reads as a gift, but 'with' just strings three pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking compassion or pity, being callous and unkind.

entries.clue: Consume copper in coppery bust (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the chemical symbol inside the jumbled letters
indicatorNotes.bust: something bust is broken, so its letters are smashed and rebuilt

annotation.walkthrough: 'Bust' reads as a sculpted head in bronze; it is the anagram instruction, broken.
annotation.definitionFit: Sense of engrossing the mind: a worry that consumes you fills your thoughts completely.

entries.clue: Watson’s colleague lacking potassium about to have a bite of meat (7)

indicatorNotes.lacking: lacking means going without, so CRICK drops its K
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so CRIC wraps round EAT

to have a bite = to eat

entries.clue: Elephant alas is transformed goddess (6,6)

indicatorNotes.is transformed: a thing transformed changes shape, as letters change into a new word

annotation.surface: Sadly, an elephant is turned into a goddess, as in some myth.

entries.clue: Join with unappreciative person penning note (9)

te, a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, fitting 'note'; it means enclosing, as a pen holds sheep.

entries.clue: I run over returning guy, perhaps predetermined? (11)

entries.clue: Army finally advance at regular intervals (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: a word's final letter comes last, the Y of armY

blocks.note: advance = early, as in advance booking

annotation.surface: At last the army advances, in regular stages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advance' reads as a military march; it is the adjective meaning ahead of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: happening annually, once every twelve months, is one kind of periodic schedule.

entries.clue: Enjoy following live act (6)

indicatorNotes.following: 'following' means coming after, so HAVE goes after BE

blocks.note: to have = to enjoy, as in 'have a good time'

annotation.surface: An audience enjoys the live act that follows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live act' reads as a stage performance; 'live' is BE and 'act' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: conducting oneself in a particular way, as in 'act your age'.

entries.clue: Mine uranium in site for processing radioactive element (11)

indicatorNotes.for processing: material sent for processing is worked into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: Uranium is mined on a site for processing into another radioactive element.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is pure nuclear industry, so the answer sits naturally in it.
annotation.definitionFit: Named example: synthetic element 99, first found in the debris of the 1952 hydrogen bomb test and named after Albert Einstein.

entries.clue: Intelligence and excellence about one restaurant worker (10)

of the first water = of the finest quality, from diamond grading

annotation.walkthrough: WATER for excellence comes from 'of the first water', the old grading of diamonds by clarity.

entries.clue: Odd bishop banned from Birmingham (3)

blocks.note: BRUM, a nickname for Birmingham, without B (bishop)

annotation.walkthrough: Brum is the everyday nickname for Birmingham, England's second city. 'Rum' is old British slang for odd.
annotation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned British slang for strange or peculiar, as in 'a rum business'.

entries.clue: Strain of bird, assumed a boiler? (5,3,3,6,2)

a kettle is a boiler of water

entries.clue: Have children, supporting area in Greek island (9)

entries.clue: Fail to justify a lot of insufficient aid (9)

entries.clue: A port cased by five United States divers (7)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like people swimming underwater; it is the old adjective meaning several or various.

entries.clue: Regret disrespectful talk holds objective back (7)

entries.clue: Computer game Place Exodus allowing going only one way (7)

blocks.note: a sim is a simulation game
Ex. = Exodus, the book of the Bible

annotation.surface: A computer game called Place Exodus that lets you move only one way.

entries.clue: Astronomer finally was the only prof we ever met (7)

entries.clue: Extreme sun unfortunately limiting red French wine (5-4-4)
